query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled pre-oxidation treatment of the boride-based component surface can form a thin, dense, and adherent alumina-rich conversion coating that serves as an effective barrier to molten-aluminum attack, thereby improving corrosion resistance in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.material_initial_state: Standardly processed boride-based components with a clean, as-fabricated surface (no special surface treatments) as currently used in the plating equipment.
generation.intervention: Expose the component to a controlled oxidation treatment by heating in air (e.g., 600°C for 2 hours) to form the protective alumina-rich layer prior to service in the molten aluminum environment.
generation.conditions: After the surface treatment, the components are exposed to molten aluminum at ~660°C (a typical hot-dip aluminum plating temperature) under static/controlled immersion conditions. The treatment is expected to remain effective as long as service temperatures are near 660°C and the oxidation layer retains its integrity without spallation during thermal cycling.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, dense, and adherent alumina-rich conversion coating on the surface of the boride-based component.
generation.mechanism: The pre-oxidation promotes the growth of an oxide barrier that reduces direct contact and interdiffusion between the molten aluminum and the underlying boride phase. This barrier minimizes the attack of aluminum on the substrate by limiting reaction kinetics and diffusion rates, thereby protecting the material from corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated components, the pre-oxidized components will exhibit reduced corrosion (as evidenced by lower weight gain, shallower penetration, and fewer corrosion-induced microstructural degradations) when exposed to molten aluminum conditions.
generation.baseline: Boride-based components produced via the standard process without any pre-oxidation or special surface treatment, showing typical signs of molten-aluminum corrosion under hot-dip conditions.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness is expected under temperature conditions around 660°C and in an oxidizing environment sufficient to form the alumina layer. The intervention might be less effective if the oxide scale is non-uniform, spalls off upon thermal cycling, or if service conditions deviate significantly from the treatment and test conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The precise improvement in corrosion resistance (quantitatively) remains uncertain without empirical data; additionally, the long-term stability of the protective layer under cyclic heating and mechanical stresses requires verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identically manufactured boride-based components. Subject one set to the pre-oxidation treatment (600°C in air for 2 hours) while keeping the other set untreated. Expose both sets to molten aluminum at ~660°C for a defined period (e.g., 24 hours). After exposure, evaluate corrosion by measuring weight gain, corrosion penetration depth, and conducting microstructural analysis via optical/electron microscopy.
measurements: Mass change before and after exposure
Microstructural integrity and oxide layer adhesion
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-oxidized (treated) samples do not show a statistically significant reduction (using an appropriate significance test, e.g., p < 0.05) in corrosion indicators compared to the untreated samples, the hypothesis that the pre-oxidation treatment improves molten-aluminum corrosion resistance will be falsified.
